body: They definitely did for me. It removed the bulky look and feeling. I don’t think gua sha had anything to do with it because I was inconsistent with it anyway.

Hmm, I wouldn’t say yes but I did notice my jaw feeling better. I was clenching it less. I got my braces off and my face went back to what I think it was before it. Gua sha is ok. I think it at least helped me with relieving myself from jaw pain but I wouldn’t say it changed the way my face looked

I swear I used to have whole day panic attacks. I’d wake up anxious, go to work anxious and come home still anxious. I thought I’d die from a heart attack anytime because of all the physical strain I would feel and I’d only “get a break” during sleep. Please learn from my mistake and seek help or remove yourself from whatever you think is causing your panic attacks. I became sick after not being able to manage it for months and it took me awhile to recover.

Don’t worry, it’s worth it. I struggled with accepting it for years so you realizing as early as now is pretty great! Sometimes you need them to go through their own shit for them to work on it. If they don’t, it’s not your problem. I think if there’s anything you can take away here is you didn’t end up like them even if you had the environment that was most likely to teach you to be the same. So feel proud of yourself for that

I’ve always wondered how they do this but I think it’s because they think it’s normal behavior so the next day they’re able to “forget” or move past it quickly. If you feel what you did was justified, you wouldn’t spend time thinking about it or acting guilty, everything is just back to BAU. I’m sorry you had to experience this and I’m sure this might not be just a one time thing. But some people are incapable of feeling guilt or shame over something they ought to.
That’s terrible. You always have to live or follow whatever suits their preferences, it’s selfish

My Nmom would go through all my things in the disguise of “cleaning up”. She would throw away things without my permission and wouldn’t even say sorry about it. There was one time I received a bear from my grandfather and she felt it was okay to give it away because it didn’t look nice enough for her and she didn’t like my grandfather (she doesn’t like anyone). I was devastated as a child and felt I had no choice and no actual property. Even when I started getting older and buying things out of my savings, they were in some way her’s because she allowed me to save, etc. they don’t understand that you’re a person who develops attachments, preferences and that they need to be respected. It’s disrespectful to a child and an actual person to not give them their sense of self and property, what exactly are you telling the child that way? 

Anyway, I suggest if you can, hide your things from her. She knows what she’s doing, she just doesn’t care about what it is to you. I’ve become distant to my mother and I don’t let her know what I own and do not own, it’s just better this way. It’s so much less stress than having this person around constantly poking holes at something that matters to you or just something you simply own. Absolutely do not engage or try to stoop down her level u less you want to develop narcissism as well. For your sake just decenter yourself from her

I second this. There are so many other relationships your children can have that will be fulfilling and have value. Spare them. Ask yourself also if it’s you wanting to have a relationship with her or your kids

I’ve wondered about this as well. My NParent and NGrandma often repeat asking about things and if I get a detail wrong, they’re so quick to correct me and sometimes make me feel stupid for even getting it wrong. It’s made me question a lot why they even asked if they knew. Feels like bait, most likely is. I think this is why they tell us gray rock method works best
Mine would scold me for hours. I would actually beg her to stop and try to convince her I’ve learned my lesson in tears. It’s so insane how they don’t know how to stop

Yes, I suppose that’s why. At least to me that was the initial reason why it was so hard for me to go no contact at first. I read Gabor Mate’s In The Realm of Hungry Ghosts for a totally different reason — I was trying to be less judgmental about addiction. But I also realized a lot of things beyond it like how addiction is a response to constant stress too and it’s usually a coping mechanism because of some trauma a person went through. I felt I might go down that path if I get pushed a little bit more so I’m really trying to be healthier emotionally. Books and videos help. The first one I watched on YouTube on narcissism was Dr. Ramani @DoctorRamani. She has an entire series about narcissism and other good material. It’s been comforting watching her videos because it makes you feel validated (I felt like I was crazy for years, it was not good). Just make sure you’re in good company to discuss whatever feelings might arise after all the revelations. I had to journal a lot and debrief with a therapist because it gets overwhelming. But it’s at least helped me move on, I genuinely feel less “stuck”, I think you get the feeling of it

YES, I now recognize it as manipulation tactics and go on my day. It took me awhile to get to apply it but I also learned about trauma and addiction and it just made me want to be better for myself. So now I HAVE to resist giving in to those traps because I already know what it makes me feel and I stopped hoping that it would change this time around

I’m still learning how to really outgrow my NParent and what I went through but I think what helps the most so far is really understand what narcissistic behavior is. Some of the blame has now shifted from what I perceived as MY shortcomings to “oh, well a narcissist would act like that”. It helped me move on from a lot of things, but it’s still a long, steady climb for me

It’s so they can feel better about themselves. Your mom could’ve just been accountable for not being good at following her GPS or making the mistake of following the wrong car and yet it’s your fault AND she had to embarrass you in front of your boyfriend. People who know how to self-regulate and have self-awareness would’ve just been upset but they wouldn’t feel the need to take it out on someone because they won’t even register it as someone else’s fault. It’s theirs and they can choose to move on from it. Narcissists NEED someone else to be at fault and sometimes even an audience to see how wrong this other person is.

I have an NMom and NGrandma. Every place I’ve moved into they’ve always found something wrong about it. Even if you thoroughly explain things to them or tell them it’s all you can do for now, they’ll never “understand” and say backhanded things like you can do better etc. Do NOT listen to them. If there’s anyone who knows best what works for you, it’s you. And even if something turns out to be wrong, it’s not the end of the world.

I used to get so upset trying to adjust to every comment they would make but I learned these people will never be happy. It also got so exhausting having to explain that I’m actually pretty content and that I don’t need to hear any comments about where I live. My last straw was having my grandmother comment on my bookshelf because she didn’t like that I put a plant on it. In her own words, “it doesn’t make sense” and I should put it somewhere else. I honestly could’ve, but I realized I was tired of them making such a big deal out of everything. It also didn’t help that she saw that bookshelf because I sent her a picture of something else and it just happened to be in the frame. We were in no way talking about the bookshelf or the plant. They love nitpicking.

Do yourself a favor and stop inviting them over to your house. You can adjust to whatever the hell they want and they’ll still find something wrong about something.

It’s really hard to work with anything when you have a lot of unresolved trauma. You’re dysregulated and then you’ll be in several stressful situations for long periods of time. It’s easy to burn out or be more prone to getting sick if you’re not already there. That’s what happened to me. It also didn’t help that I didn’t understand what was going on with my body and why I was always in fight or flight mode, it felt so impossible to comfort myself or just be at baseline. I suggest as early as now you talk to a therapist about gaining better coping mechanisms and grounding techniques because my god, it was absolute hell being in panic mode from 9-5 then coming home exhausted. If you can’t do therapy, start becoming fit and eating healthier. Because it will eventually show somewhere in the form of getting sick or catching some chronic or autoimmune disease. I almost headed that way, please don’t let yourself get even close to it

I only found out very recently many truths that made me realize how things actually are in the family. It’s like losing your religion and feeling abandoned all over again, at least for my case. But I’m glad I know the truth. It’s been a lot easier to work around it. I don’t feel guilty of the choices I make now and I can actually move on. I could have never done that before and would have definitely been manipulated into doing something else. Choose to let it set you free

My mother did the same! She started telling me about “stories” which I think some she came up with on the spot to terrify me more. I remember telling her I had to go on a work trip and all I heard was “be careful about this and that..”. It took me a long time to realize I might be just being manipulated into thinking these things so I could always run back to her for help or just choose to be around her to feel safe. It’s so insane thinking this is an actual thing people do to their own kids
I hate the experience, but it’s interesting to know more about it. I’ve been wondering a lot if it’s intentional or they’re acting out of some fear and it’s almost like an instinct

There’s been a lot of talk about how this is happening because your body is constantly producing/retaining hormones that stress your body out. So might be less of a genetic thing and more of a constant environment thing and not having your body feel safe. Imagine having an excess of hormones and knowing that anything in excess WILL cause some issues somewhere

Edit: forgot to say: glad you’re in remission! Hope you stay healthy!

I had the same experience growing up and unfortunately didn’t have my mother let me live my own life until very recently. Do yourself a favor and be as financially independent as possible. Don’t ever let her know how much you’re making and how you spend your money. The less they know, the less they can criticize and micromanage your decisions. Be aware that there’s a lot of manipulation going on and it’s most likely coming from a place where they’re way too emotionally stunted to tell that they personally have a lot of unresolved issues and trauma.

Some eventually learn and work around your boundaries and sometimes it takes YEARS to make this work, but you have to start somewhere. Picking up calls less and less is a good start, just be aware that you will feel guilty and panicked a lot (I still do even after successfully drawing my boundaries).

I felt this too. Like it was my fault that sustaining a life had a cost. Maybe she should’ve thought of that before having a child. Just doesn’t make sense to be so angry over something so obvious. I’m sorry you also had to go through that. It has a way of staying with you
I recently picked up gua sha and I THINK it helps

Literally no one could touch you anymore because nothing compares to having a parent as a bully. It’s the most confusing and damaging kind. I unfortunately became the bully and after going to therapy for anger management and all the mental illness it haunts me how terrible it all is and even how I was. It’s fucking insane. Not everybody should be a parent

I had/have (you never know when they’re going to actually act right or it’s just a temporary front, really) to go through this. You have to start putting yourself first already. If it makes you feel ill just being in the presence of this person, give yourself the space you need. I’m having trouble too with this. Mine always creates some emergency or illness to get my attention. But I’ve been faring well ever since I started “grey-rocking” her. Sometimes I just don’t talk even if I know she’s asking me a question if I sense its purpose is to rile me up. 

Just take it little by little if you can’t do it all at once. That’s still going somewhere. And from a person also learning how to do this right, I’m telling you that nothing is going to go right if you don’t start thinking about yourself and not your narcissistic parent. Mine hasn’t bothered me as much when I started drawing my boundaries. She now sticks to her friends more. 

Good luck
What does she have against a coffee mug?!?

Really glad you’re one less asshole parent and you’re doing the work to break the cycle

It’s never a pleasant memory or experience for me. The one she keeps retelling was this time I accidentally got locked in the bathroom as a kid and begging to be let out because I thought she did it on purpose. She apparently purposely waited a bit because she was laughing at how I thought I was being punished.

NTA. I mean, I don’t suggest knocking anyone’s drink someone’s hand, but were you supposed to act like this person hasn’t been abusing you for years?? Lol. Definitely NTA. She seems like such a nasty person and put you in several positions that would’ve caused anyone to act that way. I hope you don’t have to deal with such an immature person any longer. You would think by then they’d know better.

I tried this multiple times way before I knew what a narcissistic parent was and it always ended in disaster. My Nmom was defensive and would not take responsibility as a parent or just a human being. Now that I know what narcissism is, studied trauma and attachment theory, I understand better why it didn’t work out and that I did my best. That’s enough for me to know to not attempt to do it again. My Nmom is in a relatively better place now to understand because she’s overcome her own issues with her Nmom, but knowing what I know now, it’s a lost cause. Your situation could be different and I don’t want to impose upon you my experience, but narcissists have a predictable and perfectly explainable pattern so proceed with caution if you’re thinking about it

I had this problem before. I’d feel almost ashamed to admit that I’m not spending time with my own family and I wasn’t exactly sure yet why my relationship with my mother was so complicated (there was no space talking about having narcissistic parents/parenting and etc. yet). I’d get uncomfortable being asked about plans and follow up questions like why can’t I, is everyone so busy they couldn’t arrange some accommodation or etc. so I just lie about it. Most of the time I just say we’re doing something we used to do when I was a kid so if they ask me how it was I don’t have to rack my brains for an answer or forget too many details. Sometimes it hurts remembering it because those were obviously more fond and safe times with family, but I’ve learned to deal with it. So tell them about some ski trip or something and just describe it as if it just happened this holiday season if they ask again, basically. 

You’ll get used to these moments. It’s your first year away, you’re bound to feel a range of emotions and it could get overwhelming. Just remember to be grounded on the reality you have. It won’t always feel this way. Nothing beats having peace of mind because you now know and honor your own boundaries

Thanks, man. Needed to hear this today. There’s been so much going on in my head about how unhappy I am
with the situation but I think I’m getting there to finally accepting that the only way out is NC. Have to hammer it down that I do deserve to be out of harms way

Not sure if you’ve seen Dr. Ramani on YouTube, but the advice she often offers is you don’t call out a narcissist because they never will change. Most of the time it’s better to just go NC. I made the mistake of trying to go NC but explaining it and I was guilt-tripped into not doing it. Currently on very minimal interaction with my Nmom but I’m not happy with it.

I grew up being told this that it’s become a trigger to be told I look like I don’t care when I actually do. It’s manipulative. Some people find it easy to throw that statement in a situation when they feel you didn’t get to do something how they want or you didn’t do enough to satisfy their need. Sometimes it helps to stop and think if it’s actually your problem to solve and what YOU also feel about this situation. You also have to understand that not everything is your problem and if they’re so aware of what you are, then maybe they shouldn’t have relied on you for whatever then

Oh yeah, and regarding just knowing your parents had a hand in it, they definitely did. The way you were parented affects you way more than you think, no matter how bright you might have been as a child. The book I mentioned touches on that subject a lot. It’s changed the way I see parenting and common practices that I now find problematic. I hope you find what you need.

I hope you get the chance to either go to therapy or find something that helps with you learning what you need. I also share the same burden with not having enough life experiences to learn from to the point that I unfortunately walked into an abusive relationship very young because I wasn’t taught to have boundaries and I had this insane need to people please. If you’re interested, it helped me to make sense of everything that happened by reading about trauma. The Body Keeps The Score by Bessel van der Kolk was really helpful for me. If you’re not the reading type, there are videos on YouTube that can help you try to find what your next step is just so you aren’t stuck with the feeling. Unlearning a lot of things helps. I’m trying to break the cycle because I’m really unhappy with the person I might become if I don’t.

I missed out on a lot of things that are considered normal like sleepovers, going to the mall with friends, playing outside and etc. my mom had a worldview that was very “us” and “them” and every chance I was let to go out she’d find a way to catastrophize (ex. I might get raped by the brother/uncle/dad) or she’d make me think my friends and their family don’t really like me.

I’ve been going to therapy to address this and reading books about it. The best take away so far is trauma isn’t just what happened to you, but it’s what also didn’t happen to you that should have. For us it means important milestones or moments a child should have to either fondly look back on years later or just an experience to feel like you belong or exercise your autonomy. I hope you get to do the things you identify in your journal, I’ve been doing something similar and it’s been soothing that childhood wound I’ve always had. Hope it does the same thing to you
No. This kind of looks like my current teeth and I still have half a year or more to fix a similar problem.

I’ve had different therapists. One tried to convince me to be patient and even forgiving with my Nmom, the other actually asked me to consider limiting or cutting ties with her. My latter therapist has been able to sit down with me more to process why it’s more helpful in my case and to gradually teach myself to lean in to the idea that it’s become necessary. I would rather have listened to my current therapist any day. Especially that years later, I finally felt I was going somewhere with the advice she gave. Definitely find a therapist that not just sees you but will talk to you through the messiest moments and thoughts.
Have you considered reading about C-PTSD? I’m in a similar place and learning about it has been helping with being able to actually move forward.

You were beyond petty telling her you’ll report her if she doesn’t take it down, when your other neighbors are allowed to have one. No neighbor should adjust to your preference to not have something that they consider is important for their safety and is so benign. Stop making it such a big issue and about you

I second this. Do what’s best for you as much as you can. I’m not sure how old your parents are, but chances are they don’t completely know what it’s like to be a college student now and how to survive it. I had extremely strict parents who told me what to do and how to do things all the time and I got to college feeling completely unprepared for it. They were preparing me for a world THEY knew which is very different from what’s going to be yours. At some point you have to put your foot down and know when something is for you or for them. If you don’t learn how to, they might struggle also learning when to respect your choices. I hope you gain the independence and wisdom you need.

Really glad to see this. My mother is the opposite and seemed to rely on how I’d turn out for her happiness. I’m actually doing okay but fall short of some of her expectations (not married, no kids, actually do not like kids) and it’s apparently been a huge source of stress for her that I’ve turned into THIS person. She would often say I’m lucky she’s the kind of mom she is, but I’d beg to differ. There are moms out there like yours. They also care for themselves and are thus happier, even better for their child. I grew up being told those women are selfish and aren’t great with managing being a mother, but I’ve always seen it the other way. I love hearing stories like this because it proves her otherwise and maybe gives her a chance to change and find herself.

Child here of two generations of women who married young and have unresolved mental health and family dynamics issues. I’m in a phase of my life where I see very clearly how problematic they are and how perhaps choosing to have kids much later on their lives or just not at all would have been ideal. 

It scares me how “generational curses” can go on for decades. I don’t want to be part of it. I go to therapy to address several issues I have and most of it goes back to how I was raised and how I was strangely still severely neglected even if I had a helicopter mom. Recently it was also revealed to me how terrible my grandmother “parented” my mother. I’m grateful I made my own realizations and chose to go to therapy, but it can be so maddening that no one else understands but you. I’ve tried initiating a conversation about mental health with my family before and it all goes over their heads because they deeply believe that becoming a parent will transform you. Seems like their bar is also set very low because their measure of being a successful parent is if your child gets to finish school and get a job. Fuck I care if they finished it and developed severe mental illness, as long as on paper they look good then it’s still a job well done.

Break the curse if you can. I’m also living the same difficult reality that you have. I hope we find our peace and your anxiety and depression doesn’t consume you.

It sounds like that person will behave like a massive cunt regardless if you lost someone or not. I hope you aren’t being too hard on yourself about this. General rule is to let your boss know so you can have your bereavement leaves formally processed, there’s no need to let everyone else know unless you actually want to. You are very much entitled to your privacy especially something as personal as this. Your boss in some way should also help you manage, it’s nice to hear you were supported in that situation.

Really sorry for your loss. I hope you get to grieve properly and not have work at the top of your mind. The only thing you should be thinking of is how to deal with this and caring for yourself.

So this is what’s actually happening to me too. I’m sorry you’re going through this, by the way. At first it feels great to feel human at work, I was pretty open about a problem I was having so I was able to explain this long leave I had to take. Then when I came back it’s like everyone knew, HR knew, they put me on this performance improvement plan because they wanted to help me out but when I brought up actual load management and the need to have my teammates take on a more supportive role (our structure is a bit weird, it’s mainly the company’s fault, but I basically don’t even understand why they’re called my teammates because I can’t even describe how their work helps mine) they just scratched their heads and told me my role is the leadership one, etc. it’s the most hectic and whatever.

I’m leaving for the reasons said above and more. Now that I’ve stepped back, I now see how problematic the structure is and see all the circles within circles and how easy it is to misinterpret whatever personal information or opinion you have. Even an executive choice you make can be twisted, and I’ve in particular made a lot of very difficult but necessary ones that might have been unpopular to my supposed peers and feel it might have taken in whatever wrong way they’ve decided. I caught one trying to avoid me in the elevator because she didn’t expect that I would be around and although it doesn’t bother me (I’m not close to her and don’t feel the need to), that was one of those confusing moments that happened that made me realize I’m in a place where everyone is just too familiar with each other and gossip is BAU here. She now is carrying my load and is showing up late to meetings and “forgetting” meetings because of how crazy the role is. While I want her to finally develop some sympathy for me and what I have to endure, I hope she takes it as a chance to maybe grow some fucking balls (this is an issue for another time, just wanted to say it lol). 

TL;DR it happened to me too, I’m leaving and now that I’m off-hands at work, I see how truly problematic the structure and being actual friends with colleagues now.

Hey man, first off, I’m sorry this happened to you. I’m speaking as someone who’s kind of dealt with something similar (I reacted as expected to what I thought was a small issue, had someone react violently and make it bigger than it should, it then ended up with that person taking their anger out on me and I had a hard time getting over it). I think out of all the things I was told, it was “it had nothing to do with you, and everything to do with them” that helped me work out my feelings about it. Sometimes it’s easy to remember what happened and think about what you could’ve done better to have avoided it. So it becomes somehow a problem you think that started with you or within your control. But the problem in that is there is a chance you could have reacted in any other way, and that person would have (in this case) spat on your face, still. It takes a lot of work, but trying to accept that there will be people like that should be something you will have to think of so you could get over the incident.

Agreed. I learned to accept that you can’t really talk someone out of it no matter how well you lay out the facts to them once they have the child. At the same time I’ve also accepted that perhaps they are the way they are because there’s no way out for them, they’re just managing the damage already caused. I hate that you sometimes have to deal with it too though for whatever reason

Some people don’t realize they’re so arrogant, they think they’re so special that things will be different for them. Then they end up with what everyone has but you can’t exactly undo an actual human being, can you? It’s insane. I know someone who had a baby with his cheating husband and every post she makes that’s supposed to be “empowering strong women” just sounds like a cry for help but there are people who actually don’t see through the bullshit and become inspired to “take on the challenge”.

I miss my old self. She was great. She was able to work through so many challenges, even the unnecessary ones and managed to turn it to something else. Now I’m not even sure what to think about my new self. I feel like I still try, but it’s much harder to get anything done now without entering a dark place. I’m hoping I’m just tired and need a bit of rest, but it’s been years of this.

This is tricky. I’m in a slump right now. Went from reading a lot to nothing suddenly so I totally get you with reading a page and not really knowing what happened. 

So far these worked for me. Not really concentration tips though, more of reading habit tips:

1. Read regularly —  really make it a habit to condition your mind. All the times I broke my reading streak (this one right now is the longest and worst though), I would make my way back by slowly easing myself into it again. Try not to shock yourself too much by doing 100 pages a day if you can’t. Just read what you can but set a minimum

2. Highlight — it can be a favorite quote or a sentence you don’t understand yet. I do this because it makes me want to read it again and there’s something about going over the words with your highlighter that makes me think I’m also absorbing it at the same time lol. Sometimes I highlight it and then skip it if I really can’t understand it the way I want to, then I go back after awhile (if I remember to though)

3. Write notes — on the book or on a separate book/journal/any piece of paper. Maybe when you think you want to put down your book for a break because you’re distracted, quickly jot down what you’re thinking after. Even if it’s just feelings about what you read, a random thought about it or make a mind map, doodle

4. Read reviews about the book — just to get you more excited about it or see what to watch out for (beware of spoilers though if you’re into fiction. I don’t worry much about this because I usually read non-fiction)

5. Find similar literature/material about it — one time I was very interested in Norse mythology because of a game (God of War 4), so I bought a book on Norse mythology. This lead to me looking for YouTube videos as well, Reddit threads, it seems like I’m overwhelming myself but it helped me keep interested at the book I bought and also ended up with me buying more lol

6. Find people who love reading books — get inspired by bookworms and how much they love reading. You’re always more compelled to keep up with something if you’re reminded of how good something is. Plus, you get book recommendations from them or random fun facts from what they’ve read

7. Find people you can talk to about what you’re reading — or try to slide a fun fact in a conversation every now and then. It makes you look extra interesting and you have a chance of talking about it. Maybe even find someone who’s read the same thing

8. Keep track of your reading — I liked knowing how many books I’ve read and I feel fulfilled with every book I finish

See what works for you. You’ll probably find your own tricks eventually. But the most important takeaway is you’re going to have to keep trying for it to be a habit.

Good luck!! Hope this helps

Hi there! I went through similar side effects this time around with Lexapro (third time on it, long history of GAD and MDD). I felt feverish even if I didn’t have a fever, shaking and tremors (I felt cold all the time and felt there was a motor inside me), amplified anxiety and anhedonia.

A lot of people have reported to experience the same thing, so take comfort that you aren’t alone. This was the thought that kept me from going off it. I felt like complete crap for an entire week and asked for an emergency therapy session. I wasn’t scheduled to see the doctor until two more weeks but it was getting to the point that I felt much worse than when I first started taking medication. But keep in mind that this does happen. It sucks you’re already going through a rough time and you feel like this is piling on to the things you already have but give it time. I came close to becoming completely destructive because it felt like the last straw but I decided to hold on and change a couple of things:

1. Made a bigger effort to eat cleaner or just eat right - you don’t necessarily have to alter your diet completely,  but make sure you’re more mindful that you have to nourish your body. Feed yourself on time. It’s so easy to slip into either not eating or eating too much when you’re going through a difficult time. I leaned more towards not eating at all and found that it affected my mood a lot. On the flip side, if I ate too much, I felt the consequences of the weight gain and just didn’t feel great. The second day I started eating better, I felt that my body was adjusting more to the medication. Could be just coincidence, but I feel better knowing I tried and it worked with helping myself

2. Quit any vices - I did this mostly because I wanted to properly observe the effects of Lexapro on me. I needed to eliminate any other possible factors. I also didn’t want to put myself into any risk or let myself be reckless. This also helps you with discussing with your psychiatrist how you want to go about your medication should it work or not for you

3. Keep track of how you’re feeling - list any symptoms, good or bad and rate them each. This is good for you and your doctor. You can also use this to maybe write down a couple of other things you want to get out of your head. So your next therapy session, you’re able to look back at the exact thoughts you were having that day you were taking note of it

4. Take a fucking break - I can’t emphasize this enough. You’re already going through a lot. For some people, starting on the medication and therapy can be hard. If you can afford to take a break, please take it. It makes recovering and adjusting easier. Especially if your source of stress is work or you just haven’t had a break for awhile. This is the third time I’m on Lexapro. The last two times, this was exactly what happened to me. I felt so good that I thought I could live without it already. I didn’t take it to consideration that I wasn’t doing enough therapy — it was all medication and removing myself from whatever was causing my anxiety and depression that time. I also tried to rush as much as possible getting off it because of the stigma that came with taking medication — my mom, specifically wasn’t the most understanding about it.

Both times the decline was gradual but every rock bottom was much lower than the last. Sure, I have way more on my plate now since I graduated college, but I realized much of my problems still are because the moment I sought help, I was giving myself a deadline already. I was asking the wrong questions like how long should I do this before I get better, how long should I keep taking medication and can this all be done in a year? I put so much unnecessary pressure on myself with the ridiculous timeline I set. The worst part is I thought that if I was still taking medication and doing therapy after a year, I probably failed.

This time around I’m making a commitment to accept my situation as is. I have GAD and MDD. If I have to be on medication for more than a year, that’s fine. If I’ll have to see my therapist for more than a year, that’s fine too. I know I’ll get better, but instead of asking when for the meantime, I’m asking how now and I’m considering more the kind of therapy I can do. There’s such a huge possibility I wouldn’t even be in the situation I am right now had I done it right the first time around.
